questions.stem: Which VHF channel does Victoria Traffic use in Sector 1 (Juan de Fuca, Haro Strait and the southern Strait of Georgia)?
questions.explanation: RAMN 2026 Table 3-2 gives Sector 1 as Channel 11. Channel 12 is Sector 3, 74 is the Fraser River and 71 is the northern sector.

questions.stem: A tug is working in the main arm of the Fraser River above Sandheads. Which traffic channel applies?
questions.explanation: Sector 2, the south or main arm of the Fraser from Sandheads to Shoal Point, is Channel 74. Channel 71 is the northern sector and is the common mix-up.

questions.stem: A water taxi runs from Coal Harbour in Burrard Inlet to Gibsons in Howe Sound and stays inside the Iona to Gower Point line. Which sector and channel is this?
questions.explanation: Sector 3 covers the waters inside the Iona breakwater to Gower Point line, including all of Howe Sound and Burrard Inlet, on Channel 12. The Strait outside that line is Sector 1.

questions.stem: Northbound past Merry Island and on toward Cape Mudge and Johnstone Strait, which sector and channel take over?
questions.explanation: Sector 4, from the Merry Island and Ballenas line north to the Cape Sutil and Cape Caution line, is on Channel 71. Cape Mudge is a Sector 4 calling-in point.

questions.stem: How does Victoria Traffic watch vessels in Sector 4, compared with Sectors 1 to 3?
options: Radar only in Sector 4, AIS only in the others
AIS only in Sector 4, radar and AIS in the others
Radar and AIS in all four sectors
Voice reports only in every sector
questions.explanation: The note to Table 3-2 says Sectors 1, 2 and 3 are monitored by radar and AIS, and Sector 4 by AIS. That makes voice reports more important in the north.

questions.stem: In Sector 1, which station and channel handle calling-in points 1, 3, 5 and 8, such as Race Rocks and Hein Bank?
options: Vancouver Coast Guard Radio on Channel 16
questions.explanation: Table 3-2 lists Seattle Traffic on Channel 05A for calling-in points 1, 3, 5 and 8 under the co-operative system; the rest of Sector 1 is Victoria Traffic on Channel 11.

questions.stem: Which set of items makes up a position report at a calling-in point?
options: Identity, time, position and next report
Identity, cargo, draught and persons on board
Position, weather, speed and fuel on board
questions.explanation: A position report is designators A, B, C or D and N: who, when, where and the next report. Cargo, defects and route belong to the sailing plan.

questions.stem: A vessel that must report is about to leave a berth inside the zone. When is the sailing plan due, and what does it add to the basic four items?
options: On letting go; it adds only the draught
30 minutes before; it adds weather and agent
At the first calling-in point; it adds nothing
15 minutes before; it adds destination and ETA, route, cargo, defects and pollution
questions.explanation: The berth-departure sailing plan is due at least 15 minutes before and uses A, B, C or D, I, L, N, P, Q and R. A position report then follows immediately before leaving the berth.

questions.stem: Which report is made on arrival at a berth in the zone, and what is its extra item?
options: A deviation report, with the cargo
A final report, with the arrival or exit detail (K)
A sailing plan, with the route (L)
questions.explanation: The final report is made on arrival at a berth or immediately before leaving the zone, with A, B, C or D and K.

questions.stem: What is the longest a call on a traffic sector channel should normally run?
questions.explanation: RAMN Part 3 section 3.2 says calls on VTS sector frequencies should not exceed one minute. The channel is shared by every vessel in the sector.

questions.stem: A BC harbour tug on a domestic run reports to Traffic at twenty to three in the afternoon. How should the time be given?
options: 2240 UTC, as for all radio calls
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 246 requires the 24-hour system, with local time for a voyage that is not international. UTC is for international voyages.
